picks.excerpt: Patrice Desilets says Panache pulled every gen-AI asset from the 1666: Amsterdam prologue and will ship none in Early Access, admitting the team stopped noticing AI art in its own pipeline: 'we didn't even realize it was AI anymore because we were used to seeing it.' He defends the tool as a variation engine a 'small team' can't staff for — 75 versions in three seconds versus 75 illustrators.
picks.rationale: The sharpest craft warning of the week: a studio lead admits AI assets went visually invisible to his own team, which is exactly the review-gate problem every art director now has to design for.

picks.excerpt: Fenris Creations (EVE Online / EVE Frontier) has named Aslaug Arna Sigurbjornsdottir senior director of AI partnerships to push autonomous-agent work. The design hook: the studio wants EVE Frontier used as a live testbed where 'autonomous agents can be observed in a real, open and evolving economy, alongside real people.'
picks.rationale: A live MMO economy being offered as an agent testbed is a genuinely new systems-design brief — agents as inhabitants, not as production tooling.

picks.excerpt: Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick tells investors that AI tooling inside the GTA 6 publisher's studios is additive rather than substitutive — 'AI tools aren't going to replace anyone.' It's the clearest statement yet from a top-tier publisher on where it draws the line between AI-assisted production and headcount.
picks.rationale: The most quotable line a lead can take into an AI-policy meeting: a top-tier publisher putting the augment-not-replace boundary on the investor record.

picks.excerpt: Megumi Ogata, the voice of Shinji in Evangelion, calls AI voice cloning 'heartbreaking' and asks the Japanese government to step in. The push lands as synthetic-voice pipelines spread through game and anime production and Japan still lacks the AI consent terms SAG-AFTRA won in the US.
picks.rationale: Voice is the one asset class where consent terms differ by territory — a concrete reason to write AI clauses into JP-side voice contracts before the law does.

picks.excerpt: Hello Games' Sean Murray — whose studio literally shipped the poster child for procedural generation — says he is in no hurry to fold generative AI into No Man's Sky's production, comparing the industry-wide AI race to post-COVID return-to-office mandates. His pitch: 'let's just enjoy making games the way we've always made games.'
picks.rationale: The most credible possible 'not yet' — the procedural-generation studio declining the gen-AI mandate reframes adoption pressure as a schedule choice, not an inevitability.
